items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: Enoch Light had a record — he had two or three different record companies you know. And he was doing these recreations of band hits so called.

ctx.x: When you got a call to do a recording or a studio date, did you necessarily know who it was going to be for, or what the music was going to be like?

No. I know there was an exception to that that I used to do — Enoch Light had a record — he had two or three different record companies you know. And he was doing these recreations of band hits so called. And they wanted to do “I Can’t Get Started.” And the date was on a Monday morning at 10 A.M. and I hadn’t played over the weekend or anything, and they did call me, the record company, and said Dick has written, he wrote out all the notes, I don’t need them I knew them. But they said he wants you to play “I…
Are there things that stick out in your memory as great sessions, or terrible? That’s always a hard question, there’s so many of them.
